Name: 3_reviews_review_product_negative
Representative_Docs: ['“we apologize but amazon has noticed some unusual reviewing activity on this account. as a result, all reviews submitted by this account have been removed and this account will no longer be able to contribute reviews and other content on amazon. if you would like to learn more, please see our community guidelines.”it’s interesting that with ever purchase we are asked to submit a review. i am new to trustpilot and wondered if amazon used them for their reviews. i’m guessing they do not. after years of buying products from amazon and writing to occasional review, the above quoted statement is what i get if i try to write a review. it’s been a while since i called their customer service about this because, honestly, i’ve given up. on the phone they are most helpful and say that they “can fix that!” well, nope. apparently, their computer has determined we are in cahoots with the vendors. a look at the purchase history would show us to be in cahoots with all of them it that’s the case!sometimes potential customers need to know that the part actually fits “a 1997 dodge” even though amazon’s computer said it doesn’t. sometimes negative reviews have no basis. i attribute a lot of them to, what i call, 3-percenters. they would be negative if you gave them the item. why do i still give them a 5-star rating? if i do buy a product that i need to return, the process is simple. the return window is plenty long so i can determine if the item works for me. also, they have a vast selection at any price you want to pay. i’ve never read a positive review that i didn’t agree with after buying and using that product. would i buy an item having a preponderance of negative or critical reviews? probably not, but i have and been perfectly happy with my decision. moving on, amazon has invested heavily in their business. because of their distribution network it is rare that it takes more than 3 days to receive an item. often it’s less than 2! yes, i like to buy locally, but when they don’t have the item in stock and it will be “a week to 10 days” for delivery…with a higher price, to boot…i’m sorry, i’m going with amazon. in my opinion, there is no online seller that can compete with them except for maybe walmart, though their vendors often add exorbitant shipping fees. so, back to why i wrote this, my only complaint with amazon is not being able to write reviews.', "am having an interesting evening. without warning, i was banned from leaving product reviews on amazon. they accused me of receiving free goods and being paid to write reviews. what??? no one has ever paid me! nor given me free goods. (i wish!!)i actually believe they blocked me for leaving a negative review for a company that was scamming people (that happened to pay to be featured). i phoned them to review their decision, and they emailed me, (see below), saying i should email them which i did - and they sent me the same email again. then they said that i had possibly been hacked but refused to give me further details… (what?!!). was i hacked? i said i found it unlikely that someone would hack my account solely to leave reviews. what is the evidence??so, what i take from this is they only want positive reviews for some companies, and if you leave a negative one for one of their sponsored companies, they will ban you. no freedom of speech. everything being censored. buy, buy, buy, we don’t care about you, the customer…like what? i tried to resolve this and they totally refused to listen. here is their response amazon previously sent you an email explaining that we had detected unusual review and rating activity associated with this account, leading us to remove all of its reviews and ratings, and restricting it such that it is no longer able to contribute reviews, ratings, customer questions and answers, and other related community content. this account can no longer contribute content for the following reasons:-- elements of the account indicate a relationship with sellers, publishers, or other reviewers on the reviewed products.-- reviews and ratings were posted in exchange for compensation, such as gift cards, product refunds, review swaps, or free or discounted products.-- the account requested free or discounted products in exchange for reviews and ratings.-- the account was created for the primary purpose of writing reviews and ratings that violates our policies.-- an unauthorized party may have accessed this account to write reviews and ratings.as a result of your inquiry regarding this action, we reviewed this case and our decision thoroughly and have come to the same conclusion. we will not restore this account's ability to contribute with community content. we will not be answering further emails from you, nor discuss this matter further. your account will not be reinstated.like what?! is this customer service? they won’t tell me what they thing is wrong with the review…(if it was a review)…nor let me check and see if i was hacked and someone did use my account to make fake reviews. also everything they say they have banned me for is wrong! what the….? like why not just ask me to delete the one review that they didn’t like? why ban me?) i have always been 100% honest. what is ‘unusual activity?’ i have never sworn, been dishonest, never been paid, never had free goods, am a ‘normal customer that buys and pays for everything and leaves an honest review.’", 'i always like to spend some time and efforts to write unbiased reviews on amazon (or other site, such as ebay, google...etc), because i want other customers to learn from my experiences with a product or company, good or bad. like many other customer i am sure, i also use the review on amazon to decide or not to buy a product, so i also feel that it\'s normal to do the same for others people.unfortunately, after spending time and efforts to write good (sometimes long) reviews about products purchased on the site, the review get sent back to me with the following error message from amazon: "thank you for submitting a customer review on amazon. after carefully reviewing your submission, your review could not be posted to the website. while we appreciate your time and comments, reviews must adhere to the following guidelines *insert link to amazon review guidelines here*i always try to follow all their guideline to the letter when posting a product review, so i am very surprised to get this kind of answer from amazon. after sending an email to them to check about what was wrong with my reviews, here comes the surprising response from them: "we removed your review because we detected unusual review behavior on this product and are not accepting reviews of it at this time. we place limits on reviews to preserve trust in customer reviews." imagine my surprise when reading this ! and they often do that too !!! that wasn\'t the first time a legit unbiased review got rejected, while on the other hand, the product page display obviously fake reviews or short un-useful one like "i like the color". amazon, please explain how this kind of behavior blocking legit reviews from verified purchase buyer is going to "preserve trust in customer reviews" ????...so yup, as you can see amazon select the reviews they want to see posted, and block the legit ones (especially if they are negative on one of their own product page btw). you have been warned ! do not believe all review you read on amazon !! and if you feel like writing a review for something you bought on there, good luck to see it posted either !!']

Name: 108_price_cart_sale_advertised
Representative_Docs: ['i recently ordered electric mountain bike from amazon for $379. two days later my wife decided she wanted the same one as well. so i looked up the same bike and the price was now advertised for a lesser price of $353. i immediately added it to my cart. i had not yet received my bike yet at this point. i got back to my house 2 hours later and went to purchase my wife her bike but when i went to purchase the bike in the cart the price jumped back up to $379 even though it still showed $353 in the cart. i then contacted customer service to see why this was happening. they were very rude from the start of our conversation. they continued to gaslight every question i was asking. they then requested i send them screenshots of what i was trying to explain…. so i did. i was then put on hold for 15 minutes. when she came back “cs” she stated that in that two hour period the price had changed and had gone up. never explaining why it still said the lower price in my cart. i then went back to my cart after getting nowhere with customer service. i then saw that they had adjusted the price in my cart on the same bike to $455 after our conversation. this company is corrupt from the top down to the bottom. great way to appreciate a member of your store. sorry for the long story. but if you can find what you are looking for at an alternative site such as ebay i suggest you do. i have never had an issue like this with ebay… ever.', 'i tried to purchase a kindle version of a book which showed on amazon.com priced at $61.76. so i decided to buy it with one click, i wasn’t logged in so i logged in and immediately clicked on the buy with one click button as i was not expecting logging in will have any effect on the order.afterwards, i received in my email invoice with a completely different price than the one shown before ($81.59). when i brought this to the attention of amazon customer service they told me that is just a normal change in price across the time.however, then i noticed when i log out price drops back to $61.76. every single time i log into my account price becomes $81.59 and every single time i log out it drops back to $61.76. i tested this about 8-10 times and even recorded one such attempt in case they change it later so i can bring this issue to the attention of local authorities and lawmakers because if this is legal it definitely should not be in the future.i am appalled by this for two reasons:the practice itself is incredibly deceitful. in fact, since i did not notice the change in price right away and at amazon.com you buy kindle books with one click i purchased the book at an increased price and now wasted my time going through the return process. furthermore, i wonder how many shoppers might never even notice this happening and literary get scammed by amazon - i doubt that any customer expects the price of purely digital good changing after they log-in, and hence many might not check.customer service laying to customers. when i wrote an email about this to the amazon customer service their reply was that amazon prices change with time and tax rates might be different in different states.however, the price changes every time i log in log out - hence clearly the price is not a function of time but a binary function of whether i am logged in or out of my account. claiming that’s changing with time is incredibly intellectually dishonest as the fact that the price is still even of the time of this writing shown to be $61.74 shows that at least today the price was completely unrelated to time but depended solely on my logged in/out status.furthermore, this cannot be explained by taxes because when i log into my account the pre-tax price is changed as well! in fact from the order summary from my accidental purchase, i can see that the pre-tax price i was charged was $67.99. that is higher than the post vat price shown before i log in.this is really low! if amazon sets different prices based on the login of a customer they should at least be transparent about it and put a big warning sign under each price! furthermore, they should at least transparently say that price depends on the customer and not time as is the case here!all future customers of amazon should be beware of this practice! you might get billed completely different price than the one they pretend to offer!', 'i am extremely disappointed with amazon\'s sale price policies. i had seen an item i wanted on sale recently, but i missed the sale. as a result, i was watching closely to catch
